title.narrative: Somalia Enhancing Public Resource Management Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Enhancing Public Resource Management Project for Somalia is to strengthen accountability, transparency, and institutional capacity in public resource management, across participating entities. The project comprises of five components. The first component, public financial management (PFM) objective is to strengthen budget preparation, execution, and oversight for Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), Federal Member States (FMSs), and Somaliland (SL). It consists of following sub-components: (i) support essential budget execution functions; (ii) strengthen PFM in the health and education sectors; (iii) facilitate the harmonization of PFM systems between FGS and FMSs; (iv) improve budget preparation and transparency; and (v) strengthen climate-informed public investment management. The second component, domestic revenue mobilization (DRM) objective is to support the DRM priorities of FGS, FMSs, and SL to strengthen their inland revenue systems and capacity and contribute to harmonizing tax administration in FGS and FMSs. It consists of following sub-components: (i) improve tax policy capacity; and (ii) improve and harmonize inland revenue and selected customs administration systems and capacity. The third component, public sector management (PSM) objective is to support the enhancement of systems, staff skills, and effectiveness of civil service management to improve government capacity to deliver services to citizens. It consists of following sub-components: (i) strengthening the capacity of central and line Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs); and (ii) implement civil service management systems and policies, pay and grading, and pension. The fourth component, integrated governance support outlines the way in which PFM, DRM and PSM come together to support financial governance reforms and change management to guide the process. It consists of following sub-components: (i) interconnectivity of public finance and human resource (HR) systems; (ii) HR management in PFM and DRM; and (iii) change management to support DRM and PFM systems and civil service reform. The fifth component, project management, coordination, and support in delivery will support the management, coordination, and monitoring and evaluation (M and E) of project activities. It consists of following sub-components: (i) project management; and (ii) results monitoring and impact evaluation.
To strengthen accountability, transparency and institutional capacity in public resource management, across participating entities

condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I.B.1.(a) The Recipient shall, no later than 30 days from the Effective Date, establish, and thereaftermaintain throughout the period of implementation of its Respective Activities under the Project, a steering committee withmembership and terms of reference acceptable to the Association (variously, the “Project Steering Committee” or “PSC”), as furtherelaborated in the POM; which committee shall: (i) be responsible for strategic policy and decision making, technical coordinationacross FGS and FMSs, and leading on harmonization where appropriate; (ii) meet periodically, as necessary, to provide policyguidance and high-level oversight to the PCU; (iii) take decision on high level critical implementation issues under the Project;(iv) closely coordinate and share information with the Recipient's intergovernmental fiscal forum and (v) ensure inter-agencycoordination and cooperation.

title.narrative: Institutional Capacity: New potential taxpayers identified and registered

comment.narrative:
As of June 2024, a baseline of 62,943 taxpayers has been established across FGS and four FMS. Since then taxpayer registration campaigns were successfully conducted across multiple states in Somalia and FGS yielding, 1,165 new taxpayers are registered in Southwest, 1,349 â€“ in Galmudug, 1,307 in Jubaland, 1,823 in Hirshabelle, and 2,905 in FGS. The total number of newly registered taxpayers reached 8,549 representing a 13.5 % increase.
For Somaliland, the baseline of 45,159 is set as of December 2024 as reported in the MOF database.
